image:image.image:title: First-Ever Black Hole Star Discovered by James Webb Space Telescope
image:image.image:caption: An international team of astronomers using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has discovered a brand-new class of cosmic object — a black hole star — located billions of light-years away in the constellation Cetus, radiating 100 billion times more energy than any known star.

image:image.image:title: SpaceX Gears Up for a Massive Shift Into Artificial Intelligence with Starmind Satellite Network
image:image.image:caption: SpaceX is pivoting aggressively into artificial intelligence, with CEO Elon Musk predicting AI will account for 99% of company value and annual revenues of $300-500 billion by 2028, backed by a planned 1 million AI satellite network called Starmind.

image:image.image:title: Total Solar Eclipse August 2026 Crosses Greenland, Iceland, and Spain
image:image.image:caption: A total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026 swept a narrow path of totality across Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, plunging areas into midday darkness while millions across Europe witnessed a spectacular partial eclipse.

image:image.image:title: One of Britain's Finest Jurassic Fossil Collections Sold to Abu Dhabi Natural History Museum
image:image.image:caption: A rare and historically significant fossil collection from the UK's Jurassic Coast, comprising 318 specimens including new species, has been sold to the Natural History Museum in Abu Dhabi after British institutions failed to secure funding, sparking national debate over heritage preservation.

image:image.image:title: Artificial Intelligence Used to Create a Virus for the First Time in Stanford University Breakthrough
image:image.image:caption: Scientists at Stanford University have for the first time successfully designed and produced a new bacteriophage virus using AI models Evo1 and Evo2, marking a major medical breakthrough while raising urgent global biosafety concerns.

image:image.image:title: World's Most Powerful Solar Telescope Releases Clearest-Ever Images of the Sun's Surface
image:image.image:caption: The Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii has released the highest-resolution images ever obtained of the Sun's photosphere, capturing for the first time tiny Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities just 20 km wide — potentially solving the century-old mystery of why the Sun's corona is millions of degrees hotter than its surface.

image:image.image:title: More Than Half the World's Reservoirs Face Inactivation by 2060 Due to Sedimentation Crisis
image:image.image:caption: A major study reveals over half of the world's 550,000+ reservoirs face partial or complete inactivation by 2060 due to sediment accumulation, threatening water supply for more than 2 billion people and putting 26% of globally irrigated farmland at severe risk of water scarcity.

image:image.image:title: SpaceX Falcon 9 Upper Stage Crashes Into the Moon — Creating a 27-Meter Crater
image:image.image:caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket upper stage, launched in January 2025 and abandoned in a high Earth orbit after its fuel ran out, crashed into the lunar surface on August 5, 2026, creating a crater approximately 27 meters wide — providing scientists with valuable data about space debris risks to future Moon missions.

image:image.image:title: Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Impact Released Heat 17 Times Greater Than Maximum Human Tolerance, New Study Reveals
image:image.image:caption: A new study reveals the 66-million-year-old Chicxulub asteroid impact generated heat 17 times beyond human tolerance limits, instantly killing open-air dinosaurs within hours and triggering massive global wildfires — overturning the previous 'impact winter' theory of dinosaur extinction.

image:image.image:title: Volcanic Eruptions in the Pacific Ring of Fire Have Been Cooling the Earth for Centuries
image:image.image:caption: A new study from the University of Basel reveals that volcanic eruptions in the Pacific Ring of Fire caused over 22 mysterious long-term cooling periods across the past 12,000 years, with more than 80% of glacier expansion events coinciding with major volcanic events.

image:image.image:title: Africa's First Lunar Mission to Be Carried to the Moon by China in 2029
image:image.image:caption: Africa's first space exploration mission — known as BALLS (Bounced African Low Lunar Sphere) — is scheduled to be launched to the Moon's south pole in 2029 aboard China's Chang'e-8 lunar vehicle, marking a historic milestone for African space science.

image:image.image:title: The Future of Jodrell Bank Observatory at Risk
image:image.image:caption: The iconic Jodrell Bank Observatory in the UK faces closure by April 2028 due to funding cuts, threatening 28 jobs and affecting 3,000 scientists. The UNESCO World Heritage site's £2.8 million annual budget is being redirected by UKRI.

image:image.image:title: Clue Found on Nikumaroro Island Regarding Earhart's Disappearance
image:image.image:caption: Scientists prepare a new expedition to Nikumaroro Island after satellite photos reveal the 'Taraia Object' — a shape matching Amelia Earhart's Lockheed Electra — potentially solving aviation's greatest mystery after 89 years.

image:image.image:title: What Are the Mysterious 'Little Red Dots' from the Early Universe?
image:image.image:caption: New research from the University of Texas suggests the mysterious 'Little Red Dots' observed by the James Webb Space Telescope have evolved into today's star clusters, solving a cosmic puzzle about the early universe.

image:image.image:title: Orcas Observed Ramming Sunfish into Pieces
image:image.image:caption: Scientists uncover remarkable behavior of killer whales in the Gulf of California, where orcas ram giant sunfish at high speed to break their tough collagen-rich skin into manageable pieces.

image:image.image:title: Wreckage of Pan Am Aircraft Discovered on Ocean Floor After 74 Years
image:image.image:caption: Explorers discover the wreckage of Pan Am's 'Clipper Endeavor' on the ocean floor at 2,000 feet depth, 74 years after its 1952 crash off Puerto Rico that killed 52 people and led to modern airline safety briefings.

image:image.image:title: Double Star System Where Both Stars Exploded as Supernovae Discovered for the First Time
image:image.image:caption: Scientists discover the first known binary star system where both stars exploded as supernovae, using 16 years of Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope data to identify the twin remnants in the Jellyfish Nebula region.

image:image.image:title: India Becomes the Third Country in the World to Successfully Test a Private-Sector Orbital Rocket
image:image.image:caption: Indian company Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched its first private orbital rocket Vikram-1 from Sriharikota, making India the third country after the US and China with private-sector orbital launch capability.

image:image.image:title: A New Conservation Measure to Save Koalas from Extinction
image:image.image:caption: University of Queensland researchers have launched a project to cryopreserve koala eggs and sperm in liquid nitrogen at -196°C, creating a genetic backup to prevent the complete extinction of koalas.

image:image.image:title: First Medical X-Ray Images Taken in Space
image:image.image:caption: Astronauts on the private Fram2 Crew Dragon mission have successfully taken the first medical X-ray images in space, confirming a compact new X-ray device can identify health problems on future Moon and Mars journeys.

image:image.image:title: US Space Force Acquires New Electromagnetic Weapon Capable of Disabling Satellites
image:image.image:caption: The U.S. Space Force has acquired its first offensive electromagnetic weapon system, 'Meadowlands,' capable of emitting streams of electromagnetic radiation to disrupt enemy satellite signals without causing physical damage.

image:image.image:title: A Previously Undiscovered 'Mystery' Substance Found on Pluto and Titan
image:image.image:caption: The James Webb Space Telescope has detected evidence of a brand new, unidentified chemical substance on both Pluto and Titan. The mysterious molecule absorbs a specific wavelength of light and has never been found anywhere else in the solar system.

image:image.image:title: World's First Nuclear-Powered Commercial Satellite Successfully Launched into Space
image:image.image:caption: SpaceX launched the first commercial nuclear-powered satellite, BOHR, under the Transporter-17 mission. Developed by City Labs, the CubeSat uses a NanoTritium nuclear battery, enabling continuous power in deep space where solar panels are ineffective.

image:image.image:title: A New Scientific Explanation for Fermi's Paradox
image:image.image:caption: New research suggests advanced extraterrestrial civilizations may have handed over space exploration to superintelligent AI, choosing silent, efficient existence over noisy empire-building. This could explain why we see no signs of alien life despite the universe's vastness.

image:image.image:title: A New Earth-Like Planet Potentially Suitable for Life Discovered Near Our Solar System
image:image.image:caption: Astronomers have discovered GJ 3378b, an Earth-like planet 25 light-years away orbiting a red dwarf star within the habitable zone. Twice the size of Earth, this cosmic neighbor is a promising candidate for future life-searching research.

image:image.image:title: The World's Most Powerful Particle Accelerator Shut Down Until 2030 for Upgrades
image:image.image:caption: The Large Hadron Collider at CERN has been shut down for a four-year upgrade program (LS3) to become the High-Luminosity LHC. With ten times the sensitivity and triple the collision rate, scientists hope to open new frontiers in particle physics.

image:image.image:title: The First Dinosaur Fossil from Antarctica, Hidden in a Drawer for Four Decades
image:image.image:caption: A fossil forgotten in a drawer at the British Antarctic Survey for nearly forty years has been confirmed as the first dinosaur bone discovered from Antarctica — a tail vertebra from a titanosaur that lived 82 million years ago when the continent was covered in warm forests.

image:image.image:title: Swift Telescope Rescue Mission Today
image:image.image:caption: NASA launches a historic mission to save the Swift space telescope from re-entering Earth's atmosphere. The robotic spacecraft LINK, aboard a Pegasus XL rocket, will attempt the first-ever commercial robotic capture and reboost of an aging satellite.

image:image.image:title: 31 New Marine Species Discovered in the Ocean Off Brazil
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have discovered 31 new marine species in just two weeks during an expedition in international waters off Brazil. The finds include jellyfish, siphonophores, comb jellies, and giant single-celled organisms from the ocean's mysterious midwater zone.

image:image.image:title: The Heart of the Milky Way Seen Through the Euclid Space Telescope
image:image.image:caption: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has released the largest and clearest image ever captured of the center of the Milky Way, containing over 60 million stars. This visible-light mosaic could open a new era in exoplanet discovery.

image:image.image:title: Environmental Experts Oppose Plan to Crash the International Space Station into the Ocean
image:image.image:caption: Environmental experts warn that NASA's plan to deliberately crash the 400-ton International Space Station into the ocean at Point Nemo could pose severe long-term threats to marine ecosystems, with toxic chemicals, batteries, and metal debris settling on the ocean floor.

image:image.image:title: Modern Digital Technology Lends a Hand in Saving the Critically Endangered Vaquita
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have digitally reconstructed the skeletal system of the vaquita porpoise using 3D technology. With only 7-10 individuals left in the wild, this digital preservation aims to support conservation and research efforts for the world's most endangered marine mammal.

image:image.image:title: New Supernova Remnant Discovered Near the Center of the Milky Way
image:image.image:caption: A team of astronomers has discovered a new supernova remnant located near the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way. Using data from Chandra and XMM-Newton, the remnant was found in the Sgr C region, approximately 26,000 light-years from Earth.

image:image.image:title: New Air Force One Enters Service
image:image.image:caption: US President Donald Trump attended the official unveiling ceremony of the new Air Force One — a luxurious Boeing 747-8i gifted to the United States from Qatar, valued at approximately $400 million.

image:image.image:title: The World's Black Box Being Built in Tasmania
image:image.image:caption: The 'Earth's Black Box' project — proposed to be built on the island of Tasmania to store data about Earth's climate change for future generations — has been restarted and is set to be installed by December 2026.

image:image.image:title: New Details Captured from a Radiation Jet of the M87 Black Hole
image:image.image:caption: NASA X-ray space telescope reveals the most detailed X-ray data ever collected from M87's powerful radiation jet, showing unprecedented details about superluminal motion and jet dynamics spanning over a decade of observations.

image:image.image:title: Exoplanet WASP-121b: Where Rubies and Sapphires Rain Down
image:image.image:caption: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, researchers discover an ultra-hot Jupiter where rubies and sapphires rain from the sky. WASP-121b experiences extreme temperature differences, iron and gemstone rain, and winds exceeding 11,000 miles per hour.

image:image.image:title: Global Underground Fungal Network Map Revealed
image:image.image:caption: A new global map reveals the vast scale of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks — vital underground systems that store carbon, support plants, and are threatened by modern agriculture.

image:image.image:title: Artemis III Astronauts Named
image:image.image:caption: NASA announced a four-member crew for Artemis III — a high-risk 2027 crewed demonstration mission in Low Earth Orbit that will validate docking and landing procedures for future lunar landings.

image:image.image:title: MAVEN Mars Spacecraft Makes Its Final Journey
image:image.image:caption: After approximately six months of silence, NASA has officially confirmed that the MAVEN spacecraft orbiting Mars has gone completely offline, marking the end of a mission that carried out valuable observations of the Red Planet for over a decade.

image:image.image:title: Scientists Make New Discovery About the Mysterious Sound Patterns of Humpback Whales
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have for the first time identified that the mysterious deep sounds heard from coastal areas are being produced by humpback whales, revealing that whale communication abilities are far broader than previously thought.

image:image.image:title: British Paralympian John McFall Prepares to Become the First Disabled Astronaut to Orbit Earth
image:image.image:caption: British Paralympian and surgeon John McFall is on the verge of making history as the first person with a physical disability to live in space through a mission to Haven-1, the world's first proposed commercial space station.

image:image.image:title: T. Rex's Tiny Arms — An Evolutionary Sacrifice for a Powerful Skull
image:image.image:caption: A new study has solved the mystery of T. rex's disproportionately small arms, revealing they were the result of an evolutionary trade-off that allowed their skulls to evolve into a more powerful and larger form.

image:image.image:title: Evidence Found That Red Dwarf Stars Are Swallowing Planets
image:image.image:caption: Astronomers have discovered evidence that red dwarf stars are swallowing planets that orbit them, using data from the Gaia-ESO Spectroscopic Survey revealing unusually high levels of lithium in these stars' atmospheres.

image:image.image:title: Blue Origin's New Glenn Rocket Explodes During Pre-Launch Test
image:image.image:caption: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded in a massive fireball during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral Space Center in Florida on May 28, 2026, threatening NASA's Artemis lunar mission timelines and a scheduled Amazon satellite deployment mission.

image:image.image:title: Moon Base I Mission Awarded to Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin
image:image.image:caption: NASA officially selects Blue Origin for the first of three uncrewed lunar missions planned for 2026 as part of a $20 billion project to establish a lunar base, choosing the company over SpaceX to deliver equipment to the Moon's south pole.

image:image.image:title: Psyche Spacecraft Uses Mars Gravity Assist to Gain Speed
image:image.image:caption: NASA's Psyche spacecraft successfully passed by Mars on May 15, 2026, using the planet's gravity to gain crucial speed and alter its trajectory. This gravity assist maneuver will help the spacecraft reach the metallic asteroid 16 Psyche in July 2029.

image:image.image:title: Amazing Paint Coating That Provides Water from Hot Air
image:image.image:caption: A team of researchers from the University of Sydney has developed an advanced nanotechnology paint coating that can cool buildings while collecting water from the air through passive radiative cooling, offering a solution to heat and water scarcity worldwide.

image:image.image:title: A Wasp Named in Honor of David Attenborough on His 100th Birthday
image:image.image:caption: Scientists at the Natural History Museum in London have named a newly discovered genus of parasitic wasps after the world-renowned naturalist and broadcaster Sir David Attenborough on his 100th birthday.

image:image.image:title: A Tiny Object at the Edge of the Solar System Has an Atmosphere
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have discovered that a mysterious atmosphere has formed around an extremely small celestial object located at the far edge of the solar system. The object, designated (612533) 2002 XV93, is a plutino in the Kuiper Belt.

image:image.image:title: Signing of Global Pandemic Treaty Delayed Once Again
image:image.image:caption: Negotiators miss a key deadline for finalizing the Global Pandemic Treaty, with warnings that the world is still not prepared to face the next major disease outbreak, as disputes continue over pathogen information sharing and vaccine access.

image:image.image:title: An Effort to Reclassify Pluto as a Planet Once Again
image:image.image:caption: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman publicly declares that Pluto should be restored to planetary status, reigniting the decades-old debate over the dwarf planet's classification and Pluto's place in our solar system.

image:image.image:title: A New Study on the Origin of 3I/ATLAS
image:image.image:caption: Astronomers reveal that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS originated from an extremely cold and isolated region of the Milky Way and may be the oldest interstellar object ever encountered at approximately 11 billion years old.

image:image.image:title: Can a Proposed Giant Dam Across the Ocean Save AMOC?
image:image.image:caption: Scientists propose constructing a massive 51-mile dam across the Bering Strait to prevent the collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, though significant technical, environmental, and geopolitical challenges remain.

image:image.image:title: Scarlet Fever Existed in America Even Before Columbus's Arrival
image:image.image:caption: A groundbreaking genetic study reveals that Scarlet Fever was already widespread in the Americas centuries before Christopher Columbus arrived, challenging historical assumptions about the origins of epidemic diseases.

image:image.image:title: Tim Cook Steps Down as Apple CEO, John Ternus to Take Over
image:image.image:caption: Tim Cook, who led Apple following the Steve Jobs era, has decided to step down from his role as Chief Executive Officer, with John Ternus set to take over starting September 1.

image:image.image:title: Risk of Atlantic Ocean Current System Collapse on the Rise
image:image.image:caption: Latest scientific research reveals that the risk of collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is significantly higher than previously estimated, with new data putting the probability well above 50%.

image:image.image:title: Massive Mexican Government Data Theft Using Artificial Intelligence
image:image.image:caption: In what researchers describe as the world's largest cybersecurity breach, hackers used AI tools to steal hundreds of millions of sensitive records from Mexican government institutions over a 2.5-month period.

image:image.image:title: SpaceX Starlink Surpasses 10,000 Satellites in Low Earth Orbit — A Historic Milestone With Growing Concerns
image:image.image:caption: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet constellation has crossed a remarkable threshold, surpassing 10,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit as of March 17, 2026. The milestone brings unprecedented global connectivity but raises serious environmental and scientific concerns about ozone depletion, light pollution, and catastrophic collision risks.

image:image.image:title: NASA Confirms Massive Sonic Boom Over Ohio Caused by Fireball Meteor
image:image.image:caption: NASA has officially confirmed that a powerful sonic boom shook Ohio on March 17, 2026, caused by a fireball meteor blazing through the sky at over 72,000 km/h, with the event felt across Pennsylvania and New York.

image:image.image:title: NASA Confirms Massive Sonic Boom Over Ohio Caused by Fireball Meteor
image:image.image:caption: NASA confirmed that a fireball meteor caused a powerful sonic boom over Ohio on March 17, 2026, with reports heard across Pennsylvania and New York.

image:image.image:title: Ancient Ancestor of Modern Crocodiles from Over 240 Million Years Ago Discovered
image:image.image:caption: A reptile that walked across present-day Brazil during the Middle Triassic period over 240 million years ago has been discovered, revealing an ancient ancestor of modern crocodiles with a dinosaur-like appearance.

image:image.image:title: NASA Releases Clearest Images of 3I/ATLAS Taken by Mars Spacecraft
image:image.image:caption: People around the world now have the opportunity to view the clearest images of 3I/ATLAS, the third identified interstellar object passing through the solar system, captured by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

image:image.image:title: Unmanned Capsule to Be Sent for Shenzhou-21
image:image.image:caption: Three Chinese astronauts are currently 'stranded' at China's Tiangong space station after damage to their return capsule, highlighting deficiencies in China's space operations procedures.

image:image.image:title: 'The Man Who Fell to the Sun'
image:image.image:caption: An astrophotographer has successfully captured an extraordinary rare photograph of a skydiver falling freely from the sky, perfectly aligned with the surface of the Sun's face, creating an appearance as if an astronaut is falling toward the Sun.

image:image.image:title: Oldest RNA Molecules Ever Discovered Reveal Death Scene of Baby Mammoth
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have successfully extracted RNA molecules from the body of Yuka, a young mammoth that died approximately 40,000 years ago in what is now Siberia, revealing the biological processes occurring at the moment of death.

image:image.image:title: Massive Geomagnetic Storm Brings Northern Lights Even to Florida, USA
image:image.image:caption: Over the course of two nights, spectacular Northern Lights conditions were visible in unexpected locations, including areas as far south as Florida in the United States, caused by a massive dual solar storm.

image:image.image:title: Ryugu Asteroid Reveals It Once Contained Liquid Water
image:image.image:caption: With indications that large volumes of water once flowed inside the asteroid Ryugu, it appears that asteroids may have brought much more water to Earth than previously thought.

image:image.image:title: Nobel Prize-Winning Scientist James Watson, Who Contributed to Discovery of DNA Structure, Passes Away
image:image.image:caption: American Nobel laureate James Watson, one of the two scientists who discovered the structure of DNA, has passed away at the age of 97.

image:image.image:title: 3I/ATLAS Interstellar Comet: Historic Visitor from Outer Space Reaches Solar System
image:image.image:caption: Discovery of 3I/ATLAS - the third confirmed interstellar comet from another star system. Learn about this historic space discovery, its hyperbolic orbit, closest approach to Earth, and what NASA astronomers discovered about this interstellar object traveling at 221,000 kilometers per hour.

image:image.image:title: Japan's HTV-X Cargo Vehicle Launches First Mission to International Space Station
image:image.image:caption: Japan's next-generation HTV-X cargo transport vehicle successfully launched on October 25, 2025, from Tanegashima Space Center aboard the H3 rocket. Scheduled to dock with the ISS on October 29, HTV-X becomes the fourth cargo resupply vehicle serving the International Space Station, joining Russia's Progress, Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, and SpaceX's Dragon in supporting orbital operations.

image:image.image:title: Newly Discovered Asteroid 2025 TP5 Passes Closer Than the Moon: Earth's Near-Miss Event
image:image.image:caption: On October 13, 2025, the ATLAS (Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System) telescope at Mauna Loa, Hawaii, discovered a remarkable near-Earth asteroid designated 2025 TP5. Measuring approximately 16 meters (54 feet) in diameter—comparable to a 6-story building and similar in size to the 2013 Chelyabinsk meteor—this asteroid passed within 97,089 kilometers of Earth on October 15, 2025, making it closer than the Moon's orbital distance of 384,000 kilometers.

image:image.image:title: Mosquitoes Discovered in Iceland for the First Time
image:image.image:caption: Mosquitoes have been discovered in Iceland for the first time, a country previously free of mosquitoes, as the country recorded notable temperatures during the past spring season.

image:image.image:title: Solar Wind Breaks Comet Lemmon's Tail
image:image.image:caption: The latest images of Comet Lemmon (C/2025 A6) show that a portion of its tail has been 'torn off' by solar wind as it approaches the Sun after passing its closest point to Earth.

image:image.image:title: A New Method to Predict Volcanic Eruptions
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have discovered a method that can predict when a volcano might erupt again by observing magma movements beneath Mount Etna.

image:image.image:title: Large Quantity of Celtic Metal Coins Discovered in Czech Republic
image:image.image:caption: Archaeologists uncover a remarkable collection of 2,500-year-old Celtic coins, gold jewelry, and artifacts in a secret location in the Czech Republic's Pilsen region.

image:image.image:title: 2025 Nobel Prize – Chemistry
image:image.image:caption: Three scientists of Japanese, British, and Jordanian nationality awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing revolutionary metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with unprecedented applications.

image:image.image:title: 2025 Nobel Prize – Physics
image:image.image:caption: Three scientists of British, French, and American nationality awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for groundbreaking discoveries in quantum mechanics and macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling.

image:image.image:title: 2025 Nobel Prize – Physiology or Medicine
image:image.image:caption: Three scientists awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for groundbreaking discoveries about how the immune system protects us from thousands of microorganisms while preventing autoimmune diseases.

image:image.image:title: Dinosaur Fossil Found with Crocodile Bone Stuck in Jaw
image:image.image:caption: Scientists discover a new Megaraptoran dinosaur species in Argentina with a prehistoric crocodile bone preserved in its mouth, revealing ancient predatory behavior.

image:image.image:title: Sunken Port Discovery Near Egypt May Hold Clues to Cleopatra's Tomb
image:image.image:caption: National Geographic explorers have discovered a sunken port city in the Mediterranean Sea that could provide crucial clues in the ongoing search for Queen Cleopatra's hidden tomb.

image:image.image:title: 'We're Ready for Any Situation' Say Artemis 2 Astronauts
image:image.image:caption: The Artemis 2 crew intensifies training for their historic lunar mission aboard the newly named 'Integrity' spacecraft, set to launch as early as February 2026.

image:image.image:title: Silverpit Crater Confirmed to Have Been Formed by Asteroid Impact
image:image.image:caption: Scientists settle decades-long debate, confirming that the Silverpit crater beneath the North Sea was formed by an asteroid impact 43 million years ago.

image:image.image:title: Prehistoric Insects Trapped in Plant Resin Discovered for the First Time from South America
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have discovered prehistoric insects preserved in amber from South America, providing new insights into the diversification of flowering plants 112 million years ago.

image:image.image:title: World's Oldest Mummies Discovered in Southeast Asia
image:image.image:caption: Scientists have discovered 12,000-year-old mummies in Southeast Asia, making them the oldest known examples of intentional mummification in human history.

image:image.image:title: British National Pilot Joins Mars Simulation Mission Crew
image:image.image:caption: Laura Marie becomes the first British national to be selected for NASA's Mars Dune Alpha simulation program as part of the backup crew for the 378-day isolation mission.

image:image.image:title: Military Drone Mother Ship Successfully Tested
image:image.image:caption: U.S. military testing demonstrates that large drone aircraft can deploy smaller missile-like weapons, marking a significant advancement in unmanned aerial combat systems.

image:image.image:title: The Most Significant Discovery About Life on Mars So Far
image:image.image:caption: NASA's Perseverance rover has collected a rock sample containing features that could be biosignatures of ancient Martian microorganisms, potentially providing first evidence of life on Mars.

image:image.image:title: Cyanobacteria That Can Produce More Oxygen Even on Mars
image:image.image:caption: Scientists discover that extremophile Chroococcidiopsis cyanobacteria can survive Mars-like conditions and produce oxygen using Martian soil, with remarkable DNA repair capabilities.

image:image.image:title: Russia's Enteromix Cancer Treatment Vaccine Completes Preclinical Trials
image:image.image:caption: Russian authorities announce successful completion of preclinical trials for 'Enteromix' cancer treatment vaccine, claiming it reduces cancer tissue growth by 60-80%.

image:image.image:title: Changan Company Introduces Its Latest Electric Vehicle
image:image.image:caption: Chinese automaker Changan has officially unveiled its latest Nevo A06 sedan electric vehicle with industry-leading charging speeds and dual powertrain options.

image:image.image:title: China's Latest AR Helmet Providing 360-Degree Visual Range from Inside Combat Tanks
image:image.image:caption: New augmented reality helmets developed by China allow tank crews to 'see through' their armor, providing enhanced situational awareness with 360-degree visibility and integrated targeting systems.

image:image.image:title: The Shadows of the 'Black Death' That Occasionally Emerge
image:image.image:caption: The Yersinia pestis bacterium that caused the medieval 'Black Death' pandemic continues to appear in rare isolated cases, with a recent infection confirmed in California.

image:image.image:title: America's military 'space plane' takes to the skies again
image:image.image:caption: The X-37B space vehicle launches on its eighth mission with experiments in laser communication and quantum navigation technology.

image:image.image:title: Orange-colored rare shark encountered for the first time
image:image.image:caption: Researchers document the first-ever case of Xanthism combined with albinism in a Nurse Shark during a fishing competition in Costa Rica.

image:image.image:title: A previously unidentified moon of Uranus discovered
image:image.image:caption: The James Webb Space Telescope has identified a new small moon orbiting Uranus, bringing the planet's total moon count to 29.

image:image.image:title: Sony identifies weaknesses in current humanoid robots
image:image.image:caption: Sony highlights a fundamental issue in humanoid robots: limited joints create unnatural movement, calling for new structural mechanisms.

image:image.image:title: New Aspirin Alternative Shows Promise in Reducing Cardiovascular Risk
image:image.image:caption: Clopidogrel emerges as a safer alternative to aspirin for long-term cardiovascular protection with fewer gastrointestinal side effects.

image:image.image:title: The zombie-like virus spreading among rabbits in Colorado
image:image.image:caption: Wild rabbits in Colorado are being affected by a papilloma virus that causes black, tumor-like growths on their faces, giving them a zombie-like appearance.

image:image.image:title: Florida Panther: Genetic Rescue and Conservation Success
image:image.image:caption: The Florida Panther, once on the brink of extinction, has rebounded thanks to genetic rescue efforts. Despite new genes, its unique subspecies traits remain preserved.

image:image.image:title: Florida Panthers Making Remarkable Recovery from Near Extinction
image:image.image:caption: After decades of conservation efforts, Florida panthers have seen their population triple, though challenges remain for this endangered species.

image:image.image:title: Giant Einstein Ring Reveals Universe's Biggest Black Holes
image:image.image:caption: Astronomers have uncovered what may be the most massive black hole ever found, 36 billion times the mass of our Sun, hidden at the heart of the Cosmic Horseshoe galaxy.

image:image.image:title: This Tiny Spacecraft Could Race to a Black Hole and Rewrite Physics
image:image.image:caption: A visionary plan proposes sending a paperclip-sized spacecraft, powered by Earth-based lasers, to a nearby black hole within a century.

image:image.image:title: Ancient Forest Discovered Under Melting Arctic Ice
image:image.image:caption: Scientists uncover remarkably preserved 3-million-year-old forest beneath Arctic ice, providing unprecedented data on prehistoric climate conditions.
